title: 00 SU2QC Map
text:
# SU2QC Map

This is the entry note (a *map of content*: an Obsidian term for a note whose job is to link to everything else).
Open **Graph view** to see the whole "brain", or open [[SU2QC Map.canvas|the canvas]] for the hand-laid-out picture.

## The research goal

All packages serve the Genesis Phase-I proposal *AI-Accelerated Non-Abelian Gauge Dynamics on Quantum Hardware*
(see [[Genesis Phase-I proposal]]): simulate [[SU(2) lattice gauge theory]] on quantum computers, with AI and
machine learning helping at every step.

## The packages (all SU2QC repositories on github.com/digonto10602, read for this map)

| package | one-line job | state on 2026-10-06 |
|---|---|---|
| [[genesis-su2-lgt]] | first starter: a pure-gauge two-plaquette benchmark on every backend | dormant since 2026-08-13 (v1.1.0) |
| [[su2qc-skqd]] | Project 2: sample-based Krylov diagonalization of SU(2) with quarks, run on IBM hardware | active; 2×2 hardware run done; XY4 gain did not replicate; 2×3 on IBM measured NO-GO (6 Oct); next route is Quantinuum (access email not sent) |
| [[su2qc-jepa]] | Gauge-JEPA-P v2: a JEPA world model of string breaking, with a Krylov-chain hardware carrier | active; week 1 of 8; J0 PASS; J1 FAIL for all 9 finished training runs (semigroup row), jobs 013–014 queued |
| [[SU2ZX]] (`genesis-su2-zx-observables`) | compiler study on a pure-gauge chain, then the verified one-plaquette-with-matter code and the GI-cost campaign | paused since 2026-09-10; campaign at C0 partial |
| [[su2qc-trotter]] | Clifford+T resources for one plaquette Trotter step ($j_{\max}=\tfrac12$, 12-qubit encoding) with CUDA-Q; lean 22-qubit design | done 2026-09-27; all 7 Perlmutter CI jobs PASS |
| [[su2qc-paulo-code]] | the reference 34-qubit Clifford+T plaquette circuit (notebook + QASM) that su2qc-trotter starts from | static files, not a git repository |
| [[su2qc-qcadvantage]] | "SU(2) torus frontier run": one-qubit-per-plaquette SU(2) on tori, exact + noisy + MPS, toward a quantum-advantage test | cloud phase M1–M6 done 2026-10-06 (branch `claude/modest-mayer-kh4s6b`); 4 decisions wait for you before cluster work |

title: CIPSI and classical support controls
text:
# CIPSI and classical support controls

**Plain words.** To show the quantum device adds value, compare its subspace with subspaces a classical computer
could choose at the *same size*: **CIPSI** (grow the subspace by adding the configurations that perturbation theory
says matter most), **BFS** (add neighbours by Hamiltonian connectivity), random sets, an exact oracle, and an ML
ranker. This comparison is su2qc-skqd's primary endpoint P1. Code: [[skqd.controls]], [[skqd.ml]].

title: Clean-shot fraction
text:
# Clean-shot fraction

**Plain words.** The probability that one run (shot) of a circuit happens with no error at all, $f$. SKQD cost scales
like $1/f$ shots (worse, $1/f^2$, at very small $f$). su2qc-skqd's go/no-go bar is $f\ge0.1$. Estimated from hardware by
the reference-string statistic or a mixture estimator; the CF_traj work showed the hit statistic actually tracks the
*ideal-sample* fraction ([[Result - CF_traj clean-fraction re-ruling]]). Code: [[skqd.device_req]], [[skqd.idle]].
backlinks: Result - 2x3 on ibm_kingston is a measured NO-GO
Result - client-side XY4 gain did not replicate

title: Clifford+T and T-count
text:
# Clifford+T and T-count

**Plain words.** Fault-tolerant quantum computers will run only a fixed, finite gate set: the **Clifford** gates
(H, S, CNOT — cheap on error-corrected hardware) plus the **T gate** (a $\pi/4$ phase — expensive, because it needs
*magic-state distillation*). Arbitrary rotations must be approximated by long H/S/T sequences (**synthesis**, e.g.
gridsynth) to a chosen error $\epsilon$. The **T-count** (number of T and T$^\dagger$ gates) is the standard cost metric.
[[su2qc-trotter]] counts it for one plaquette Trotter step: 1162 T (Paulo's 34-qubit circuit) versus 424 T (the lean
22-qubit design) at $\epsilon=10^{-6}$ per rotation ([[Result - lean 22-qubit plaquette Trotter step]]).

title: Codewords and the Gauss-law decoder
text:
# Codewords and the Gauss-law decoder

**Plain words.** Each physical state is assigned a fixed bit string (its *codeword*; 12 bits at 2×2). After
measurement, the decoder checks every string against [[Gauss's law]] and link consistency and either returns the
physical state or rejects the string. Random strings pass only ~0.15 % of the time, so the codewords act as a
built-in distance-2 error-*detection* code. Code: [[skqd.codec]].

title: Decoherence (T1 and T2)
text:
# Decoherence (T1 and T2)

**Plain words.** $T_1$: how long a qubit keeps its energy (an excited $|1\rangle$ decays to $|0\rangle$). $T_2$: how long it keeps
its phase. $T_2^\*$ (measured by a Ramsey experiment) includes slow drifts; $T_2^{\rm echo}$ removes them. Long, serial
circuits are limited by idle time, which is why the 2×3 SKQD circuit fails on superconducting devices. Code:
[[skqd.idle]], [[skqd.coherence]].

title: Dynamical decoupling
links: Result - client-side XY4 gain did not replicate
text:
# Dynamical decoupling

**Plain words.** While a qubit waits idle it slowly loses its phase. Inserting carefully timed pulse sequences (e.g.
**XY4**: X, Y, X, Y) into the idle windows cancels much of that drift. In [[su2qc-skqd]], client-side XY4 raised the
clean fraction 2.8× on ibm_kingston on 2 Oct, but the gain did not replicate on 6 Oct ([[Result - client-side XY4 gain did not replicate]]).
backlinks: Result - client-side XY4 gain did not replicate

title: Exact diagonalization
text:
# Exact diagonalization

**Plain words.** Write the Hamiltonian as a matrix and compute its eigenvalues directly. Feasible for the small
systems here (82, 677, 1 727 states) and used as the "truth" every quantum or ML result is checked against:
[[skqd.exact]], [[genesis_su2.exact]], [[su2qc_jepa.physics.dynamics]].

title: JEPA world model
text:
# JEPA world model

**Plain words.** A *joint-embedding predictive architecture* (JEPA) learns by predicting the **summary** (latent
embedding) of a future observation from the summary of the current one, instead of predicting the raw data. A
*world model* is a model that predicts how a system evolves given actions.

In [[su2qc-jepa]]: encoder MLP ($24\to128\to128\to16$) maps a noisy observation vector to a 16-dimensional latent; a
GRU predictor advances it under actions (time steps at given couplings); grounding heads read energy, $C_{\rm string}$,
$P_{\rm meson}$, $P_{\rm baryonic}$ and a flag rate from the latent; [[SIGReg]] prevents collapse; a semigroup check
requires two half-steps to equal one full step. Code: [[su2qc_jepa.models.jepa]], [[su2qc_jepa.models.train]].

title: Krylov subspace and Lanczos
text:
# Krylov subspace and Lanczos

**Plain words.** Start from one state and repeatedly apply the Hamiltonian (or time evolution); the states you
generate span a *Krylov subspace*, which captures the low-energy physics surprisingly fast. **Lanczos** builds an
orthonormal basis of it in which $H$ becomes tridiagonal (only diagonal and next-to-diagonal entries).

[[su2qc-skqd]] uses time-evolved Krylov states to generate samples ([[skqd.krylov]]). [[su2qc-jepa]] uses Lanczos to
compress the dynamics into $K=12$ states that fit on 12 qubits ([[Krylov-chain carrier]], [[su2qc_jepa.physics.dynamics]]).

title: Krylov-chain carrier
text:
# Krylov-chain carrier

**Plain words.** [[su2qc-jepa]]'s trick to put the plaquette dynamics on hardware cheaply. [[Krylov subspace and Lanczos|Lanczos]]
compresses the relevant dynamics into $K=12$ basis states with a tridiagonal Hamiltonian; each basis state is
encoded as one excited qubit in a line of 12 ($|0\dots010\dots0\rangle$). Nearest-neighbour hops then implement the
dynamics: 22 CZ per Trotter step, 34 / 56 / 100 / 188 CZ for $r = 1, 2, 4, 8$ steps — a real depth ladder. States with
zero or two excitations are flagged as errors. Code: [[su2qc_jepa.physics.chain]]; qubit line chosen by [[su2qc_jepa.twin.layout]].

title: L12 encoding
text:
# L12 encoding

**Plain words.** [[SU2ZX]]'s 12-qubit encoding of the [[Shared 2x2 plaquette]] (3 qubits per vertex), with
exact gauge-invariant Strang circuits built from block unitaries. Exact and leak-free, but about 2 156 two-qubit gates
per Strang step after compilation — far too deep for current hardware, which is why the later packages built cheaper
carriers ([[Krylov-chain carrier]], skqd codewords). Code: [[su2qc.encodings.l12]], [[su2qc.circuits.strang_l12]].

title: Leakage-safe data splits
text:
# Leakage-safe data splits

**Plain words.** When training on physics data, test examples must come from coupling values never seen in training
(split by parameters, not by rows), otherwise the model looks better than it is. [[skqd.ml]] splits by
$(\lambda, \text{lattice})$; [[jepa gate J0]] checks that no held-out trajectory appears in training.

title: Loschmidt echo
text:
# Loschmidt echo

**Plain words.** Run a circuit forward and then its exact inverse. Without noise you return to the starting state
with probability 1; the measured return probability therefore estimates the *global fidelity* $F$ of the noisy run.
[[su2qc-qcadvantage]] uses it to check the noise model (echo $F$ within 3–13 % of the predicted $\prod(1-\epsilon)$), and
found that rescaling local observables by the global $F$ over-corrects them. [[su2qc-trotter]] uses a cross-technique
echo (one circuit forward, the other backward) to show the lean and reference circuits are the same unitary.
backlinks: Result - lean and reference circuits agree on GPUs
Result - qcadvantage noise mitigation at N=12

title: Noise models and digital twin
text:
# Noise models and digital twin

**Plain words.** A *digital twin* is a simulator configured with a real device's calibration (gate errors, $T_1$, $T_2$,
readout) so you can rehearse a hardware run. Qiskit **Aer** is the simulator used. Warning learnt in su2qc-skqd: the Aer
model at the echo $T_2$ was 5.1× too optimistic for the clean fraction. Code: [[skqd.noise]], [[su2qc_jepa.twin.noise]], [[su2qc_jepa.twin.run]].
backlinks: Result - qcadvantage noise mitigation at N=12

title: Quantum kernel methods
links: Result - genesis QML surrogate is a negative result
text:
# Quantum kernel methods

**Plain words.** Encode each data point as a quantum state; the overlap between two states is a similarity
("kernel") that a classical support-vector machine can use. Finite shots make each overlap noisy. In
[[genesis-su2-lgt]] the quantum-kernel surrogate became unstable at 512 shots ([[Result - genesis QML surrogate is a negative result]]).
backlinks: Result - genesis QML surrogate is a negative result

title: Readout error and confusion matrix
text:
# Readout error and confusion matrix

**Plain words.** Measuring a qubit sometimes returns the wrong bit. The *confusion matrix* records how often each
prepared value is read as each outcome; it is measured with simple preparation circuits and used to correct counts.
In the ibm_kingston run the smallest diagonal entry was 0.9417. Code: [[skqd.hardware]].

title: Ritz values and certified bounds
text:
# Ritz values and certified bounds

**Plain words.** Diagonalize $H$ in a subspace and the lowest eigenvalue $E_R$ (the *Ritz value*) is never below the
true ground energy $E_0$. The residual $r_H = \|(H-E_R)\psi_R\|$ measures how far the approximate eigenvector is from a
true one, which gives a guaranteed interval:

- Weinstein: some exact eigenvalue lies in $[E_R - r_H,\ E_R]$;
- Kato–Temple: the tighter $[E_R - r_H^2/(\alpha - E_R),\ E_R]$ given a lower bound $\alpha$ on the next level.

Both are the ground-state interval only if the nearest level is the ground state (the *gap assumption*). Used in [[skqd.skqd]].

title: SIGReg
text:
# SIGReg

**Plain words.** A JEPA can "cheat" by mapping every input to the same latent (collapse), which makes prediction
trivial. *SIGReg* (sketched isotropic Gaussian regularization) penalises latents whose distribution is far from a
round Gaussian, keeping them spread out. Its weight is one rung of [[su2qc-jepa]]'s ablation ladder (jobs 003, 004).
The J1 gate checks the *effective rank* of the latent ($\ge 8$ of 16).
backlinks: Result - J1 ladder fails on the semigroup row

title: Sample-based Krylov quantum diagonalization (SKQD)
text:
# Sample-based Krylov quantum diagonalization (SKQD)

**Plain words.** A hybrid quantum–classical way to find ground energies ([[Yu et al. 2025 SKQD]]; parent method
SQD, [[Robledo-Moreno et al. 2024]]). The quantum computer prepares time-evolved states
$e^{-iHk\Delta t}|b_0\rangle$ and is measured in the configuration basis; the distinct, valid configurations form a
subspace $B$; a classical computer diagonalizes the exact $H$ inside $B$. The quantum part only *chooses* the
subspace, so the energy is always an upper bound ([[Ritz values and certified bounds]]).

**The fairness trap.** If the subspace is a large fraction of the sector, random strings find it too — then the
device contributes nothing ([[van Rossum et al. 2026]]; [[Result - 2x2 SKQD run on ibm_kingston]]).

Implemented in [[su2qc-skqd]]: [[skqd.krylov]], [[skqd.skqd]], [[skqd.controls]].

title: Tensor networks (MPS and TEBD)
links: Result - qcadvantage MPS frontier at N=48
text:
# Tensor networks (MPS and TEBD)

**Plain words.** A compressed way to store quantum states of 1D-like systems as a chain of small tensors (a
*matrix product state*, MPS); **TEBD** evolves them in time with Trotter steps. They give classical reference results
for systems too big for [[Exact diagonalization]]. Planned in [[genesis-su2-lgt]] (gate G9, `docs/TENSOR_NETWORK_IDEAS.md`), not started.
Used in [[SU2ZX]] v0.4.0 (plaquette chain to $N=32$) and in [[su2qc-qcadvantage]] ([[su2torus.mps]], quimb `CircuitMPS`), where the
**bond dimension** $\chi$ (the size of the tensors, i.e. how much entanglement the MPS can hold) was raised from 32 to 256 at
$N=48$ to find where the classical answer stops converging ([[Result - qcadvantage MPS frontier at N=48]]).
backlinks: Result - SU2ZX v0.4.0 compiler and MPS study
Result - qcadvantage MPS frontier at N=48

title: Transpilation and CZ count
text:
# Transpilation and CZ count

**Plain words.** *Transpiling* rewrites a circuit into the gates and qubit connections a specific device supports.
Two-qubit gates (CZ on IBM Heron) are the main error source, so the CZ count after routing is the key cost. skqd's
original budget (≤ 250 CZ per coarse step at 2×2) failed (gates L3, S2) and was amended to a clean-fraction criterion.

title: Trotter and Strang splitting
text:
# Trotter and Strang splitting

**Plain words.** $e^{-iHt}$ is hard to build as a circuit when $H$ has non-commuting parts. Split $H=\sum_\gamma H_\gamma$
and apply each part for a short time in sequence: first-order **Trotter** $\prod_\gamma e^{-iH_\gamma\Delta t}$;
second-order **Strang** uses a symmetric order (error $\propto \Delta t^3$ per step). su2qc-skqd's "coarse step" applies
each term once for time $k\Delta t$ with $\Delta t = \pi/W$ ($W$ = spectral width). [[genesis-su2-lgt]] gate G3 studies
product formulas in Qiskit.

title: ZX-calculus circuit optimization
text:
# ZX-calculus circuit optimization

**Plain words.** The ZX-calculus rewrites a quantum circuit as a graph of simple "spiders" and simplifies it with a
small set of exact rules; **PyZX** is the standard library. "Basic" and "Teleport" are two PyZX simplification
strategies. Used in [[SU2ZX]] v0.4.0 to choose the cheapest compiled circuit for each case, and in your SU(2) circuit
lab (PyZX `basic_optimization` cut two Strang repetitions from 118 to 94 ECR gates; `full_reduce` made it worse, 180).
backlinks: Result - SU2ZX v0.4.0 compiler and MPS study

title: Zero-noise extrapolation
links: Result - qcadvantage noise mitigation at N=12
text:
# Zero-noise extrapolation

**Plain words.** Error mitigation (not correction): run the same circuit with the noise deliberately amplified, for
example by replacing each gate $G$ with $G G^\dagger G$ (**gate folding**, noise factor 3) or $G(G^\dagger G)^2$
(factor 5), then fit the measured value against the noise factor and extrapolate back to factor 0.
In [[su2qc-qcadvantage]] ([[su2torus.noise]]) folding at factors 1, 3, 5 cut the error of $\langle H_E\rangle$ by
5.8–15.5× in 4 of 4 tested configurations at $N=12$ ([[Result - qcadvantage noise mitigation at N=12]]).
backlinks: Result - qcadvantage noise mitigation at N=12

title: Baryon-number sectors
text:
# Baryon-number sectors

**Plain words.** The number of quarks minus the half-filling value is conserved by the Hamiltonian, so the Hilbert
space splits into independent blocks (sectors) labelled by baryon number $B$. On the [[Shared 2x2 plaquette]]:
2 / 20 / 38 / 20 / 2 states for $B = -2..2$. Each sector can be diagonalized or simulated on its own.

title: Clebsch-Gordan coefficients
text:
# Clebsch-Gordan coefficients

**Plain words.** The numbers that say how two spins combine into a total spin. Needed to build the colour-singlet
states at each site ([[Intertwiner (dressed-site) basis]]). Implemented in [[skqd.su2]] and [[su2qc_jepa.physics.su2]].

title: Electric basis
text:
# Electric basis

**Plain words.** Describe each link by its electric-field quantum numbers $|j, m, n\rangle$ (Peter–Weyl states). Electric
energy is then diagonal (cheap); the magnetic plaquette term is not. All SU2QC packages build their basis this way at
$j_{\max}=\tfrac12$. Compared with alternatives in [[genesis-su2-lgt]] ([[genesis_su2.encodings]]).

title: Fuzzy gauge theory
text:
# Fuzzy gauge theory

**Plain words.** A qubitization that replaces the continuous SU(2) group manifold by a "fuzzy" (finite-matrix)
sphere, keeping more of the group structure than a plain truncation ([[Alexandru et al. 2023 fuzzy]]). In
[[genesis-su2-lgt]] it was deliberately **not** implemented: the source definition was not fixed enough, so it is
marked BLOCKED-SOURCE-DEFINITION rather than guessed.

title: Gauss's law
text:
# Gauss's law

**Plain words.** At every site, the colour charge flowing in through the links must equal the charge sitting on the
site. Only states obeying this everywhere are physical; the rest are artefacts of the encoding.

$$G_a(x)\,|\text{phys}\rangle = 0, \qquad [G_a(x), H] = 0 .$$

Every package checks $[G_a, H]=0$ numerically (gates E1, J0, G7.2–G7.4). On hardware, Gauss's law becomes a free
error check: measured strings that violate it are rejected ([[Codewords and the Gauss-law decoder]]).

title: Intertwiner (dressed-site) basis
text:
# Intertwiner (dressed-site) basis

**Plain words.** Instead of storing every link's full state, one stores at each site only the combination of
incoming/outgoing flux and quarks that is a colour singlet (allowed by [[Gauss's law]]). The label of which singlet
is the *intertwiner* $\iota_x$. A basis state is $|\{j_\ell\},\{n_x\},\{\iota_x\}\rangle$. This gives exactly the
physical states — 82 / 1 727 / 37 165 on 2×2 / 2×3 / 2×4.

[[su2qc-skqd]]: [[skqd.vertex]], [[skqd.basis]]. Uses [[Clebsch-Gordan coefficients]].

title: Jordan-Wigner mapping
text:
# Jordan-Wigner mapping

**Plain words.** A rule that turns fermion operators (which anticommute) into qubit operators by attaching a string of
$Z$ gates that tracks how many fermions sit "before" a given mode. The ordering choice matters and is frozen in each
package's conventions ([[su2qc_jepa.physics.conventions]]; skqd: "JW order = site order").

title: Kogut-Susskind Hamiltonian
text:
# Kogut-Susskind Hamiltonian

**Plain words.** The energy operator of lattice gauge theory in continuous time ([[Kogut and Susskind 1975]]). Four kinds of term:

$$H = \underbrace{\tfrac{g^2}{2}\sum_\ell E_\ell^2}_{\text{electric}} \;-\; \underbrace{\tfrac{1}{2g^2}\sum_P (W_P + W_P^\dagger)}_{\text{magnetic (plaquette)}} \;+\; \underbrace{m\sum_x (-1)^x n_x}_{\text{mass}} \;+\; \underbrace{\text{hopping}}_{\psi^\dagger U \psi}$$

$g$ is the gauge coupling; $E_\ell^2 = j_\ell(j_\ell+1)$ is the electric energy on link $\ell$; $W_P$ is the
[[Plaquette and Wilson loop]]; the mass term uses [[Staggered fermions]]; the hopping term moves a quark across a
link while updating the link field $U$.

In [[su2qc-skqd]] see [[skqd.hamiltonian]]; in [[su2qc-jepa]] see [[su2qc_jepa.physics.plaquette]] (written in units of $g_E$).

title: Link truncation (j_max)
text:
# Link truncation (j_max)

**Plain words.** The electric field on a link can take infinitely many values (spins $j = 0, \tfrac12, 1, \dots$).
A computer must stop somewhere: $j_{\max}$ is the largest spin kept. All SU2QC packages use $j_{\max}=\tfrac12$
(each link is either empty or carries one unit of flux); $j_{\max}=1$ is used as a check of the truncation error
(152 states instead of 82 on the [[Shared 2x2 plaquette]]).

title: One-qubit-per-plaquette SU(2) model
text:
# One-qubit-per-plaquette SU(2) model

**Plain words.** The cheapest known exactly gauge-invariant form of pure SU(2) gauge theory in 2+1 dimensions
([[Ciavarella et al. 2026]]): keep only $j=0$ and $j=\tfrac12$ on every link of a triangular lattice and use
[[Gauss's law]] to eliminate the links, so that each **plaquette** becomes one qubit. The plaquettes form a honeycomb
graph; on a torus (periodic boundaries) there are $N$ plaquette qubits:

$$H=\frac{3g^2}{16}\sum_{\langle pq\rangle}(1-Z_pZ_q)\;-\;\frac1{g^2}\sum_p\Big[\prod_{q\in nb(p)}c(n_q)\Big]X_p,\qquad c(0)=1,\ c(1)=\tfrac12 .$$

The first sum is the electric energy (a cost on every bond between plaquettes in different states); the second flips a
plaquette with an amplitude that depends on its neighbours (this neighbour dependence is what makes it non-Abelian).
Setting $c\equiv1$ gives the **abelian twin**, the transverse-field Ising model, used as a control.
Code: [[su2torus.lattice]], [[su2torus.hamiltonian]] in [[su2qc-qcadvantage]].

title: Pauli decomposition
text:
# Pauli decomposition

**Plain words.** Writing a Hamiltonian as a weighted sum of products of Pauli matrices $I, X, Y, Z$ — the native
language of qubits. [[genesis-su2-lgt]] keeps one canonical Pauli decomposition ([[genesis_su2.pauli]]) and generates every
backend from it.

title: Plaquette and Wilson loop
text:
# Plaquette and Wilson loop

**Plain words.** A plaquette is the smallest closed square of links. The Wilson loop $W_P = \mathrm{Tr}(U_1U_2U_3^\dagger U_4^\dagger)$
multiplies the link fields around it; it is the magnetic-energy term of the [[Kogut-Susskind Hamiltonian]] and
the term that lets flux circulate. In [[su2qc-skqd]] the plaquette term is a 30-CNOT pair rotation on 2×2.

title: Quantum link (rishon) encoding
text:
# Quantum link (rishon) encoding

**Plain words.** Replace each link by a few fermion modes ("rishons") at its two ends, with a fixed total occupation;
the link operators become products of fermion operators ([[Chandrasekharan and Wiese 1997]]). Implemented and
validated at small scale in [[genesis_su2.encodings]]; marked as the proposal candidate for the next matched-Hamiltonian study.

title: SU(2) lattice gauge theory
text:
# SU(2) lattice gauge theory

**Plain words.** A gauge theory describes forces carried by fields that live *between* particles. "SU(2)" is the
symmetry group (2×2 unitary matrices with determinant 1); it is the simplest **non-Abelian** group, meaning the
force carriers themselves carry charge, as in the strong force (whose group is SU(3)). *Lattice* means space is
replaced by a grid: matter on the sites, gauge fields on the links between sites.

**Why SU2QC uses it.** It keeps the hard features of QCD (non-Abelian charges, confinement, string breaking) while
being small enough for today's quantum computers.

Used by every package: [[genesis-su2-lgt]], [[su2qc-skqd]], [[su2qc-jepa]]. Hamiltonian form: [[Kogut-Susskind Hamiltonian]].

title: Staggered fermions
text:
# Staggered fermions

**Plain words.** A way to put quarks on a lattice: one fermion component per site, with the sign of the mass
alternating between even and odd sites, $m\sum_x(-1)^x n_x$. Filled odd sites play the role of the "Dirac sea";
moving a quark creates particle–antiparticle pairs. "Two-colour" means each site holds up to two quarks (the two
SU(2) colours). Qubit mapping uses [[Jordan-Wigner mapping]].

Used in [[su2qc-skqd]] ([[skqd.fermions]]) and [[su2qc-jepa]]. Absent from [[genesis-su2-lgt]] (pure gauge).

title: String breaking
text:
# String breaking

**Plain words.** Pull two static colour charges apart and a "string" of electric flux forms between them; its energy
grows with length. At some point it becomes cheaper to create a quark–antiquark pair from the vacuum, which snaps the
string into two mesons. Watching this happen in real time is a flagship target of quantum simulation.

[[su2qc-jepa]] learns the dynamics from the stretched-string state (observables $C_{\rm string}$, $P_{\rm meson}$, $P_{\rm baryonic}$).

title: Thermalization and canonical typicality
links: Result - qcadvantage thermalization and the beta=0 states
text:
# Thermalization and canonical typicality

**Plain words.** A closed quantum system started far from equilibrium usually ends up looking *thermal*: local
observables settle to the values of a thermal state $e^{-\beta H}/Z$ whose inverse temperature $\beta$ is fixed by the
starting energy. The **thermal anchor** is that predicted late-time value; the **decohered value** is the
infinite-temperature ($\beta=0$) value, i.e. what a fully scrambled or fully noise-destroyed state would give.
**Canonical typicality** computes thermal values without diagonalizing $H$: apply $e^{-\beta H/2}$ to a few random
vectors and average (statistical error shrinks with the number of vectors).

In [[su2qc-qcadvantage]] ([[su2torus.thermal]]) this is how an observable is judged useful: if the anchor sits close to
the decohered value, hardware noise and real physics cannot be told apart. See
[[Result - qcadvantage thermalization and the beta=0 states]].

title: Cross-package opportunities
links: Result - GI-cost campaign stalled at C0
Result - client-side XY4 gain did not replicate
text:
# Cross-package opportunities

*These are Claude's own observations from reading the repositories side by side (2026-10-05), not decisions you have made.*

1. **Reuse skqd's ibm_kingston knowledge in jepa's hardware campaign.** su2qc-skqd found that the Aer model at the
   echo $T_2$ was 5.1× too optimistic, and (updated 6 Oct) that the device's no-DD clean fraction changed by a factor ≈ 2
   between two days, larger than any [[Dynamical decoupling]] effect. [[jepa gate J3]] relies on an Aer twin of the
   same device class — it should inherit skqd's $T_2^\*$ bracket and plan same-day controls, not one-day A/B tests.
   Links: [[Result - client-side XY4 gain did not replicate]], [[su2qc_jepa.twin.noise]], [[skqd.idle]].
2. **A three-way cross-check of the 82-state Hamiltonian.** su2qc-jepa already matches SU2ZX's `su2qc` to $7\times10^{-14}$.
   Mapping su2qc-skqd's 2×2 Hamiltonian (lattice units) onto jepa's units of $g_E$ would tie all three codes
   together. See [[Shared 2x2 plaquette]].
3. **The chain carrier is ~25× cheaper per step than an SKQD coarse step** (22 CZ vs ≈588 CZ). If the 2×3 SKQD run
   stays out of reach, a Krylov-chain-style circuit for SKQD support generation might be worth one planner question.
   Links: [[Krylov-chain carrier]], [[Result - 2x3 needs a different device]].
4. **Shared calibration guard.** skqd keys submissions on calibration content; jepa's
   [[su2qc_jepa.hardware.ibm]] has a dry-run-first budget guard. One shared module would avoid two
   implementations drifting.
5. **The GI-cost question is half-answered elsewhere.** SU2ZX's campaign asked what exact gauge invariance costs on
   hardware (GI arm vs playback). su2qc-skqd's structured codeword circuits (≈588 CZ, exact, leak-free) and su2qc-jepa's
   chain carrier (22 CZ/step) are two more data points on the same plaquette; a one-page comparison could close the
   campaign's C-gates without new QPU time. Links: [[Result - GI-cost campaign stalled at C0]].
6. **genesis-su2-lgt as a regression test.** Its two-qubit benchmark is cheap; running it on each new IBM backend
   before a real session is a fast health check.
7. *(added 2026-10-06)* **Three 12-qubit encodings of one plaquette now exist** — [[L12 encoding]] (3 qubits per vertex,
   with quarks), skqd codewords, and su2qc-trotter's 3 qubits per link (pure gauge). su2qc-trotter's flag/bright-pair
   tricks (4 rotations, Margolus Toffolis on don't-care inputs) might cut the L12 Strang step cost; worth one question
   to a planner. Links: [[Result - lean 22-qubit plaquette Trotter step]].
8. *(added 2026-10-06)* **qcadvantage's MPS frontier and SU2ZX's MPS study measure the same thing on different
   models.** SU2ZX v0.4.0 scaled a plaquette chain to $N=32$ at short times; [[su2qc-qcadvantage]] found MPS fails after
   2–3 steps at $N=48$ on a 2D torus. Quoting both in one table would show reviewers why 2D matters.

title: Lessons that travelled
links: Decision - jepa 001 numbered artifacts and Graphify
text:
# Lessons that travelled

| lesson | where it was learnt | where it is now built in |
|---|---|---|
| Aer seeds shot $k$ with `seed + k`, so runs seeded `seed`, `seed+1` overlap in $N-1$ of $N$ shots and every quoted spread was void | [[SU2ZX]] GI-cost campaign, session c060_p0_20260909_5 (seeds 500/501: 1 023 shift matches of 1 024) | [[su2qc_jepa.twin.run]] spawns independent seeds; a row of [[jepa gate J0]] tests it |
| generated code documentation covered a different package than the one under test, letting the twin-seed defect through review | SU2ZX v0.6.3 | [[Graphify code graph]] rebuilt every session and freshness-checked in CI ([[Decision - jepa 001 numbered artifacts and Graphify]]) |
| a raw residual against the twin correlates ~perfectly with the exact error, so a "Spearman ≥ 0.7" bar is meaningless without label-free baselines | su2qc-jepa plan audit | [[jepa gate J3]] must report raw_twin, flag_rate, jepa_self, jepa_t0 |
| at 2×2, random strings through the decoder already reproduce $E_0$ (sector saturation) | [[su2qc-skqd]] H0_2x2 | garbage-only and random-equal-size baselines are now mandatory in skqd reports |
| the device model can be 5× off; measure first | su2qc-skqd kingston pilot | skqd: pilot before every main run; jepa plan: 1.5-minute pilot measures the real rate |
| an "all outputs verified at 1e-10" flag was too strong: default-tolerance `Operator.equiv` never checked routed outputs, and PyZX's QASM rounding added ~1e-10 errors | [[SU2ZX]] v0.4.0 audit | explicit atol/rtol and independent routed-output checks; skqd verifies circuits against its own IR to < 1e-10 |
| a builder can silently miss physics (route 1 omitted dressed-vertex recoupling factors) — only a second independent route catches it | [[SU2ZX]] Section 8, solutions/0.5.0.md | every package now builds the Hamiltonian two ways |
| one Hamiltonian, many backends: never re-type physics per backend | [[genesis-su2-lgt]] | skqd's backend-independent IR ([[skqd.circuits_ir]]); jepa's two-route builder |
| a one-day hardware A/B test is not a result: the device's no-DD clean fraction doubled in 4 days, more than the XY4 effect | [[su2qc-skqd]] H0_ddrep (6 Oct) | skqd's 2026-10-06 report withdraws the XY4 note as written; [[Cross-package opportunities]] item 1 |
| code that only runs on a GPU on the cluster can fail where the laptop never shows it (CPU network, GPU data) | [[su2qc-jepa]] jobs 002–007 | a device test in the CPU and CUDA cases; a 2-epoch GPU smoke job before long runs |

title: Shared 2x2 plaquette
text:
# Shared 2x2 plaquette

The single physical system that [[SU2ZX]] Section 8 verified first and that [[su2qc-skqd]] and [[su2qc-jepa]] both study:

- one square plaquette (4 sites, 4 links, open boundaries), [[SU(2) lattice gauge theory|SU(2)]] gauge field truncated at
  $j_{\max}=\tfrac12$ ([[Link truncation (j_max)]]);
- two-colour [[Staggered fermions]] on the 4 sites;
- [[Gauss's law]] imposed exactly → **82 physical states**;
- [[Baryon-number sectors]]: $2/20/38/20/2$; the 38-state sector is where the [[String breaking|string-breaking]] dynamics live;
- at $j_{\max}=1$: 152 states.

| | SU2ZX Section 8 (first, 7 Sept) | su2qc-skqd | su2qc-jepa |
|---|---|---|---|
| what is computed | exact dynamics, then GI-vs-playback circuit cost | ground energies by [[Sample-based Krylov quantum diagonalization (SKQD)]] | real-time dynamics learned by a [[JEPA world model]] |
| qubits on hardware | 12 ([[L12 encoding]]) | 12 (codewords, [[Codewords and the Gauss-law decoder]]) | 12 ([[Krylov-chain carrier]], one-hot) |
| circuit cost | ≈ 2 156 two-qubit gates per Strang step | one coarse step ≈ 588 CZ, 44 µs on ibm_kingston | 22 CZ per Trotter step; 34–188 CZ for $r=1..8$ |
| two independent builders | [[su2qc.ham.route_spinnet]] vs [[su2qc.ham.route_gausskernel]] | [[skqd.hamiltonian]] vs [[skqd.fullspace]] | route A vs route B in [[su2qc_jepa.physics.plaquette]], plus cross-check with SU2ZX |
| hardware so far | none (twin only) | ibm_fez, ibm_kingston | none (emulated) |

All three agree on the state count and sector split. su2qc-jepa ↔ SU2ZX are numerically cross-checked
($7.3\times10^{-14}$); su2qc-skqd has **not** been cross-checked against either (different units: lattice units with
$g^2$, $m=3g^2/16$, versus units of $g_E$) — see [[Cross-package opportunities]].

title: Decision - qcadvantage open questions before the cluster
links: Result - qcadvantage thermalization and the beta=0 states
text:
# Decision - qcadvantage open questions before the cluster

Four decisions that `notes/STATUS.md` of [[su2qc-qcadvantage]] (6 Oct 2026) leaves to you. **Not yet decided.**

1. **Initial state at $N=48$–$64$.** The plan prescribes the stripe state, but on tori with even $L_1$ it sits at
   $\beta=0$ (thermal = decohered), so it cannot separate physics from noise. Recommended: the SU(2) vacuum
   ($\beta\approx1.4$) or an odd-row state. Evidence: `reports/m3_physics.md` §3; [[Result - qcadvantage thermalization and the beta=0 states]].
2. **Open-lattice electric term.** The code uses the bond form; METHODS' $3n_p$ form differs on open lattices
   (string $E_E(0)=4.41$ vs $5.88$). Evidence: `reports/audits/m1_audit.md`.
3. **Trotter step size.** $2\delta t/g^2=0.9$ (plan M6) departs strongly from $e^{-iHt}$: at $N=12/16$, step 8, Trotter
   $\langle H_E\rangle$ is 0.54 versus exact 0.31 (fractions of $E_\infty$). Decide $\delta t$ before cluster thermal-anchor
   work. Evidence: `reports/audits/m6_audit.md`.
4. **Tags.** Push `m1-done` … `v0.1-pre-cluster` from a machine with tag-push rights (`git push origin --tags`).

title: Genesis Phase-I proposal
text:
# Genesis Phase-I proposal

*AI-Accelerated Non-Abelian Gauge Dynamics on Quantum Hardware* (NMSU / BNL / UMD) — the parent document of every
SU2QC package. It asks for SU(2) lattice gauge theory Hamiltonians, quantum circuits and physical observables on real
quantum hardware, with AI/ML accelerating the workflow.

| package | which part of the proposal it serves |
|---|---|
| [[genesis-su2-lgt]] | backend-portable starter; encoding comparison; first QML surrogate |
| [[su2qc-skqd]] | hybrid quantum–classical spectroscopy with ML-assisted configuration ranking, on hardware |
| [[su2qc-jepa]] | AI world model of real-time gauge dynamics; label-free hardware error signals |
| [[SU2ZX]] | verified one-plaquette-with-matter physics core; ZX/QML circuit work |
| [[su2qc-trotter]] (with [[su2qc-paulo-code]]) | fault-tolerant (Clifford+T) circuit cost of the plaquette Trotter step |
| [[su2qc-qcadvantage]] | a path to a beyond-classical SU(2) dynamics run on today's hardware |

# IBM Quantum Open Plan

title: How to use this vault
text:
# How to use this vault

## Opening it

1. The vault lives at `~/Projects/su2qc-Brain`, next to the repositories it is built from.
2. In Obsidian: *Open folder as vault* → choose the `su2qc-Brain` folder.
3. Open [[00 SU2QC Map]]. Press the graph icon (or `Ctrl/Cmd+G`) for **Graph view**.

Graph view colours are preset (in `.obsidian/graph.json`): packages, modules, gates, concepts, hardware, papers and
results each get their own colour. Useful graph filters (type them in the graph's search box):

- `tag:#package` — only the packages
- `path:Modules/skqd` — only the su2qc-skqd code
- `tag:#gate -tag:#pass` — gates that have not passed
- `[[Gauss's law]]` — everything that mentions Gauss's law

**Local graph** (right-click a note → *Open local graph*) shows one note and its neighbours; this is often more
readable than the full graph.

## What is generated and what is hand-written

- `Modules/` and `Gates/` are **generated** from the repositories by `_tools/build_vault.py` (module docstrings,
  import statements, gate tables). Do not edit them by hand; re-run the builder instead.
- Everything else (packages, concepts, hardware, papers, results, decisions, hubs) is **hand-written** and safe to edit.

## Refreshing after the repositories change

```bash
cd ~/Projects/su2qc-Brain/_tools
python build_vault.py --repos ~/Projects --overwrite-hand   # reads every su2qc-* repo plus genesis-su2-lgt and the SU2ZX checkout
python export_jsonl.py                       # rebuild _export/su2qc_brain.jsonl
```

A Claude Code session can do this for you: "read `_tools/README.md` and refresh the vault".

## Using it for AI

`_export/su2qc_brain.jsonl` has one JSON record per note (a *JSONL* file: one JSON object per line, the usual
input format for training and retrieval pipelines). Each record has `id`, `title`, `type`, `package`, `status`,
`links` (the notes it points to), `backlinks` and `text`.

- **Retrieval (recommended).** *Retrieval-augmented generation* (RAG) means the model looks up the most relevant
  notes when it answers. Point Claude Code, Hermes or any RAG tool at the vault folder or the JSONL file, and an
  agent starting a new SU2QC session gets the project map, the conventions and the latest gate status in a few
  thousand tokens.
- **Agent memory.** Add a line to a package's `CLAUDE.md`: "read `~/Projects/su2qc-Brain/00 SU2QC Map.md` and the notes it
  links before planning".
- **Fine-tuning (limited).** About 200 notes is far too small to teach a model physics by fine-tuning. It *is*
  enough for an evaluation set (questions whose answers are in the notes) or as a seed for generated
  question–answer pairs. The real training data in these projects are the measurement records and trajectories in
  the repositories themselves (see [[su2qc-jepa]] datasets and [[su2qc-skqd]] `data/hardware/`).

title: su2qc_jepa.data.records
text:
# su2qc_jepa.data.records

Module of [[su2qc-jepa]] · `src/su2qc_jepa/data/records.py` · 183 lines

## What it does (from the module docstring)

> Measurement records and the observation estimator shared by all three sources.
>
> A *record* is what a carrier returns for one (state, measurement setting): a
> dictionary of bitstrings -> counts, plus metadata.  The *estimator* turns the
> records of one time point into the observation vector o_t.  Exact states, the
> Aer twin and the hardware all go through the same estimator, which is what
> makes the three sources comparable.
>
> Two carriers are supported:
>
> * ``diagonal``: a Z-basis measurement of a diagonal encoding of the 82-state
>   basis (this is how the exact source and the L12 twin look: every primary
>   observable is a function of the measured configuration).  Records are counts
>   over basis indices.  Flags are leakage flags (zero for the exact source).
> * ``chain``: the Krylov-chain carrier (one-hot encoding of K Krylov vectors).
>   Records are counts over K-bit strings for settings Z and X (optionally Y).
>   Z gives the Krylov populations and the excitation flag; X gives the real
>   parts of the Krylov coherences; together they give every physical observable
>   through O_K = Q_K^T O Q_K (O diagonal in the configuration basis).

## Uses

[[su2qc_jepa.physics.chain]] · [[su2qc_jepa.physics.dynamics]] · [[su2qc_jepa.physics.observables]]

## Used by

# su2qc_jepa.data.trajectories

Module of [[su2qc-jepa]] · `src/su2qc_jepa/data/trajectories.py` · 264 lines

## What it does (from the module docstring)

> Trajectory generator: exact dynamics + emulated finite-shot observations + split manifest.
>
> A trajectory is an initial gauge-invariant state followed by n actions.  An action
> is one time step of duration dt at couplings (cM, cH, cB) (cE = 1 in units of g_E);
> a mass quench is a trajectory whose cM changes at a given step.  Every time point
> carries the clean exact observables (the JEPA target) and a finite-shot
> observation (the JEPA context), built through the same estimator used for twin
> and hardware records (see records.py).
>
> Two coupling *families* are scanned, because the physics-setup measurements of
> 1 Oct 2026 showed that the mass dependence of the P-A window is weak while the
> strong-coupling resonance at mu* = 3/8 is sharp:
>
> * family "onfam"  - on-family points (cH, cB) = (1/(2 g_E), -1/(4 g_E^2)) with g_E scanned;
>                     held out by g_E (the dynamics depend strongly on g_E, weakly on mu).
> * family "strong" - strong-coupling points cH = |cB| = 0.02 (the P-S regime) with mu scanned
>                     around the resonance; held out by mu.
>
> Splits are by rule, never by row.  The manifest records every parameter and a
> checksum of the arrays.

# su2qc_jepa.hardware.ibm

Module of [[su2qc-jepa]] · `src/su2qc_jepa/hardware/ibm.py` · 202 lines

## What it does (from the module docstring)

> IBM Quantum submission path with a dry-run-first, budget-guarded discipline.
>
> Nothing here talks to a QPU unless ``submit(..., confirm=True)`` is called with an approved
> budget file.  The sequence Claude Code must follow (CLAUDE.md, hardware rules):
>
> 1. ``dry_run``  - transpile to the backend's ISA on the chosen qubit line, count CZ and
>                    two-qubit depth, estimate QPU seconds, write a manifest with circuit hashes.
> 2. human reads the manifest and edits configs/hardware_budget.yaml (approved: true).
> 3. ``submit``   - re-checks the manifest hash against the budget file, the running ledger of
>                    QPU seconds, takes a calibration snapshot, submits one Sampler job, records
>                    job id + options + snapshot in evidence/hardware/jobs/<job_id>.json.
> 4. ``collect``  - fetches results, writes raw counts (immutable) and usage.
>
> The quantum-seconds estimate is a *prior*; the pilot job's measured usage replaces it.

# su2qc_jepa.jobs

Module of [[su2qc-jepa]] · `src/su2qc_jepa/jobs.py` · 116 lines

## What it does (from the module docstring)

> Job requests for the Perlmutter worker — decisions/004 (queue introduced in decisions/003).
>
> A job is a numbered YAML file `jobs/NNN_<slug>.yaml` on the `main` branch, written on the laptop by
> `scripts/jobs/enqueue.py` and never edited afterwards.  A worker (scripts/worker/worker.py, started by
> `scrontab` on Perlmutter) pulls `main`, runs jobs addressed to it at the
> exact commit named in the file, and pushes status and outputs to the separate `results` branch:
>
>     results/<NNN>/status.json      state, timings, node-hours, output sizes, worker host
>     results/<NNN>/log.txt          last lines of the job's output
>     results/<NNN>/outputs/<path>   the files listed under `outputs:` (e.g. runs/v1_base/...)
>
> The laptop never connects to Perlmutter; the worker never pushes to `main`.
>
> Safety: every command step must be `python scripts/<allowed>.py ...` with the script in
> ALLOWED_SCRIPTS, so a worker only ever runs this repository's own entry points.

title: su2qc_jepa.localrun
text:
# su2qc_jepa.localrun

Module of [[su2qc-jepa]] · `src/su2qc_jepa/localrun.py` · 340 lines

## What it does (from the module docstring)

> Resource-aware, self-healing execution on the laptop (decisions/004).
>
> The laptop (64 GB RAM, 6-core i7-8750H, GTX 1060 Max-Q not used) is shared with other Claude sessions, so
> every computation from this project goes through `scripts/run.py`, which uses this module to:
>
> 1. **classify** the command: heavy (estimated above `heavy_minutes` at the granted threads, or asks for a GPU)
>    → always sent to Perlmutter through the job queue; light → may run here;
> 2. **admit** it only if the machine has room *now*: MemAvailable minus the request stays above a reserve kept
>    for other programs, and the 1-minute load plus the requested threads leaves free cores; only one su2qc
>    computation at a time across all sessions (a lock file).  If there is no room it waits (bounded), then
>    sends the job to Perlmutter if it can be queued;
> 3. **run it capped**: lowest CPU/I/O priority, thread caps for every math library, a memory ceiling (cgroup via
>    `systemd-run --user --scope` when available, otherwise an address-space limit), a wall-clock limit, and
>    `oom_score_adj = 1000` so that under memory pressure the kernel kills this job, never another session;
> 4. **heal**: a resource failure (memory kill, address-space exhaustion, timeout) is retried once with a larger
>    memory ceiling if the machine has room, otherwise the job is sent to Perlmutter; a program error (an
>    ordinary exception) is not retried — it is a bug and is reported with the log tail.
>
> Every attempt is appended to `.local_runs/ledger.jsonl` (git-ignored) with its probe, limits and outcome.

## Uses

[[su2qc_jepa.compute]] · [[su2qc_jepa.jobs]]

## Public names

title: su2qc_jepa.models.jepa
text:
# su2qc_jepa.models.jepa

Module of [[su2qc-jepa]] · `src/su2qc_jepa/models/jepa.py` · 188 lines

## What it does (from the module docstring)

> Gauge-JEPA-P v2: classical encoder + action-conditioned predictor + SIGReg + grounding heads.
>
> Definitions (plain words):
> * encoder  E_theta : observation o_t (noisy, finite shots)  -> latent s_t in R^d
> * predictor P_phi  : (s_t, a_t, ..., a_{t+k-1})             -> predicted latent for time t+k
> * JEPA loss        : || P_phi(s_t, a) - E_theta(o^clean_{t+k}) ||^2 ; the target is the encoder
>                      of the *clean* future observation (exact expectation values), never the
>                      observation itself.  By default there is no moving-average target: collapse is
>                      prevented by SIGReg.  With JEPAConfig.ema_target = tau the target latent comes from an
>                      exponential-moving-average copy of the encoder under stop-gradient (I-JEPA style);
>                      SIGReg then acts on the context latent only.
> * SIGReg           : LeJEPA's sketched isotropic Gaussian regulariser - random 1-D projections of
>                      the latent batch are pushed toward N(0,1) with an Epps-Pulley characteristic-
>                      function statistic.  (arXiv:2511.08544)
> * grounding heads  : linear maps from the latent to known physical quantities (energy, string
>                      Casimir, channel weights, flag rate), used in training only, so the latent is
>                      identifiable and encoder/predictor cannot co-adapt into a trivial code.
> * semigroup loss   : P(s, [a, a]) ~ P(P(s, [a]), [a]) - the predictor must compose like time evolution.

## Used by

`su2qc_jepa.models.train`

## Public names

`JEPAConfig`, `MLP`, `ActionPredictor`, `sigreg_loss`, `effective_rank`, `GaugeJEPA`

title: su2qc_jepa.physics.chain
text:
# su2qc_jepa.physics.chain

Module of [[su2qc-jepa]] · `src/su2qc_jepa/physics/chain.py` · 265 lines

## What it does (from the module docstring)

> The Krylov-chain hardware carrier (one-hot / unary encoding of the Lanczos basis).
>
> Given the tridiagonal Krylov Hamiltonian H_K = sum_k alpha_k |k><k| + sum_k beta_k (|k><k+1| + h.c.),
> encode the K Krylov vectors as the K single-excitation states |k> = |0..010..0> of K qubits on a
> line.  In the single-excitation sector
>     |k><k|            -> n_k = (1 - Z_k)/2
>     |k><k+1| + h.c.   -> (X_k X_{k+1} + Y_k Y_{k+1})/2
> so H_K becomes a nearest-neighbour XY chain with site-dependent fields, and
> exp(-i H_K t) is realised by a second-order (Strang) product formula whose
> entangling cost is 2 CZ per bond per step on IBM hardware.
>
> The circuit conserves the excitation number, so any shot outside the single-
> excitation sector is a detectable error ("excitation flag"), the chain analogue
> of the gauge-leakage flags of the L12 encoding.
>
> `chain_sector_unitary` gives the exact K x K action of the *ideal* Trotter circuit
> inside the single-excitation sector (no 2^K simulation needed), which is the
> noiseless reference against which hardware and twin records are compared.

## Uses

[[su2qc_jepa.physics.dynamics]]

title: su2qc_jepa.physics.conventions
text:
# su2qc_jepa.physics.conventions

Module of [[su2qc-jepa]] · `src/su2qc_jepa/physics/conventions.py` · 81 lines

## What it does (from the module docstring)

> Frozen conventions for the hard-core SU(2) Kogut-Susskind plaquette with
> two-colour staggered fermions.  These follow the SU2QC physics-setup notes
> (9 Sept 2026) so that every number produced here can be compared with the
> project's verified `su2qc` code.  Do not edit without a new ADR in docs/.
>
> Geometry (one square plaquette, open boundaries):
>
>     v3=(0,1) ---l2---> v2=(1,1)
>        ^                 ^
>        |l1               |l3
>        |                 |
>     v0=(0,0) ---la---> v1=(1,0)
>
> Links are stored in the order (la, l1, l2, l3) = indices (0, 1, 2, 3).
> Loop orientation for the plaquette: U_sq = U_a U_3 U_2^dag U_1^dag.
> Staggered phases: eta_x = 1, eta_y(n) = (-1)^{n_x}; product around the loop = -1.
> Jordan-Wigner mode order: (v0-, v0+, v1-, v1+, v2-, v2+, v3-, v3+) where the
> colour index is the magnetic number m in {-1/2, +1/2} of the fundamental.

## Used by

`su2qc_jepa.data.trajectories` · `su2qc_jepa.gates.j0_data` · `su2qc_jepa.physics.observables` · `su2qc_jepa.physics.plaquette`

text:
# su2qc_jepa.physics.plaquette

Module of [[su2qc-jepa]] · `src/su2qc_jepa/physics/plaquette.py` · 520 lines

## What it does (from the module docstring)

> Hard-core SU(2) Kogut-Susskind plaquette with two-colour staggered fermions.
>
> Two independent constructions are provided and cross-checked in the tests:
>
> * **Route A (vertex singlets, block tensors)** - `PlaquetteModel` builds the
>   gauge-invariant (GI) basis as a configuration basis labelled by the four link
>   spins and the four site occupations, with the colour structure fixed by the
>   unique singlet at every vertex.  Hamiltonian matrix elements are computed by
>   applying each term to the block tensor of a basis state.  Works for any j_max.
> * **Route B (full gauge-redundant space)** - `FullSpaceOperators` builds every
>   operator as a sparse matrix on the full link (x) matter space and lets the
>   tests check (i) that H commutes with all Gauss-law generators, (ii) that the
>   route-A basis vectors are annihilated by the generators and (iii) that
>   Q^dag H Q reproduces route A.  Practical for j_max = 1/2 (160,000 states).
>
> Units: H is measured in units of g_E (see conventions.Couplings).

[[su2qc_jepa.physics.conventions]] · [[su2qc_jepa.physics.su2]]

Module of [[su2qc-jepa]] · `src/su2qc_jepa/repo/artifacts.py` · 254 lines

## What it does (from the module docstring)

> Numbered artifacts: plans, prompts, reports, decisions and figures.
>
> Rule (decisions/001): everything a person reads that is *produced* during the project —
> a plan, a prompt for a Claude Code session (written by the planner or by Claude Code itself),
> a report, a decision record, a figure — is a numbered, append-only file in its series folder:
>
>     <series>/<NNN>_<slug>.<ext>        NNN = 000, 001, ... allocated only by `new_artifact`
>
> * numbers are unique, start at 000 and have no gaps;
> * the slug is lowercase letters, digits and `-`;
> * Markdown artifacts carry YAML front matter with `id`, `title`, `series`, `created_utc`,
>   `author`, `milestone`, `status`, `supersedes`, `superseded_by`;
> * a revision is a *new* number with `supersedes: <old id>`; the old file's only permitted edit
>   is `status: superseded` and `superseded_by: <new id>`;
> * each series has an `INDEX.md` regenerated by the tool (never hand-edited).
>
> Living documents (one file edited in place, versioned by git) are *not* numbered: README,
> CLAUDE.md, docs/PHYSICS.md, docs/CLAIMS.md, docs/PREREGISTRATION.md, docs/PAPER_OUTLINE.md,
> configs, STATE.json.  Machine records (evidence/*.json, raw hardware counts) keep their UTC stamps
> and job ids because they are immutable and referenced by hash.

Module of [[su2qc-jepa]] · `src/su2qc_jepa/repo/graph.py` · 59 lines

## What it does (from the module docstring)

> Helpers around the Graphify code graph (graphify-out/graph.json).
>
> Graphify (PyPI package `graphifyy`, command `graphify`) parses the repository locally with
> tree-sitter — no LLM, no API key in code-only mode — into a graph of files, classes, functions,
> imports, calls and Markdown headings, clusters it into communities and writes
> `graphify-out/graph.json` and `graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md`.  This module only *reads* those
> files: it counts nodes/edges/communities, lists the most connected nodes, and decides whether a
> committed graph is structurally identical to a fresh rebuild (ignoring the commit stamp and the
> community assignment, which are not structure).

## Public names

title: su2torus.hamiltonian
text:
# su2torus.hamiltonian

Module of [[su2qc-qcadvantage]] · `su2torus/hamiltonian.py` · 246 lines

## What it does (from the module docstring)

> Minimal (one qubit per plaquette) SU(2) Hamiltonian, arXiv:2608.28752.
>
> Basis convention (docs/METHODS.md, section 2): qubit p <-> plaquette p; |1> = excited
> (n_p = 1, Z_p = -1). Basis index b = sum_p n_p 2**p (Qiskit little-endian).
>
>     H_E = (3 g^2 / 8) sum_p ( 3 n_p - sum_{q in nb(p)} n_p n_q )
>         = (3 g^2 / 16) sum_{bonds} (1 - Z_p Z_q)
>     H_B = sum_p a_p X_p,   a_p = -(1/g^2) prod_{q in nb(p)} c(n_q),  c(0)=1, c(1)=1/2
>     Abelian twin (abelian=True): c == 1, i.e. a_p = -(1/g^2).
>     H_B^A / H_B^B : the X terms on sublattice A (up) / B (down) only.

## Used by

`su2torus.exact` · `su2torus.observables`

## Public names

`flip_amplitude`, `electric_diagonal`, `split_sparse`, `build_sparse`, `flip_pauli_terms`, `build_pauli`, `cheb_recur`, `axpy`, `apply_h`

title: su2torus.lattice
text:
# su2torus.lattice

Module of [[su2qc-qcadvantage]] · `su2torus/lattice.py` · 90 lines

## What it does (from the module docstring)

> Plaquette graph of the triangular lattice (= honeycomb graph).
>
> Conventions (see docs/METHODS.md, section 1):
> - Triangular-lattice sites (i, j), 0 <= i < L1, 0 <= j < L2.
> - Each cell (i, j) owns two triangular plaquettes:
>     kind 0 = "up"   triangle with vertices (i,j), (i+1,j), (i,j+1)      -> sublattice A
>     kind 1 = "down" triangle with vertices (i+1,j), (i,j+1), (i+1,j+1)  -> sublattice B
> - Plaquette index p = 2*(i*L2 + j) + kind, so n = 2*L1*L2 plaquettes.
> - up(i,j) shares a link with down(i,j), down(i-1,j), down(i,j-1).
>   Periodic: indices wrap mod L1, L2. Open: neighbours outside the patch are dropped.
> - A hexagon is the set of 6 plaquettes touching one triangular-lattice site (i,j):
>   up(i,j), up(i-1,j), up(i,j-1), down(i-1,j), down(i,j-1), down(i-1,j-1),
>   returned in cyclic order (consecutive entries share a link, last-first too).

## Public names

`HoneycombTorus`, `initial_state`

# su2torus.noise

Module of [[su2qc-qcadvantage]] · `su2torus/noise.py` · 140 lines

## What it does (from the module docstring)

> Noisy emulation and error mitigation (PLAN M4; API fixed by tests/acceptance/m4).
>
> Noise model (Aer convention, k qubits, d = 2**k): after each gate
>     E(rho) = (1 - p) rho + p Tr_k(rho) (x) I/d,
> with p = p2 on every cx / rzz and p = p1 on every 1-qubit gate, plus a symmetric readout
> error r on every qubit. Predicted global fidelity: the probability that no gate applies a
> non-identity Pauli, F = prod_gates (1 - eps), eps = p (1 - 1/d^2) (process infidelity):
> eps_2q = 15 p2 / 16, eps_1q = 3 p1 / 4.

title: su2torus.trotter
text:
# su2torus.trotter

Module of [[su2qc-qcadvantage]] · `su2torus/trotter.py` · 90 lines

## What it does (from the module docstring)

> Trotter circuits (docs/METHODS.md, section 3).
>
> Step ordering, with U_X(t) = exp(-i H_X t):
>     order 1:  U_step(dt) = U_BB(dt) U_BA(dt) U_E(dt)      (U_E acts first)
>     order 2:  U_step(dt) = U_E(dt/2) U_BA(dt/2) U_BB(dt) U_BA(dt/2) U_E(dt/2)
> Equality is required up to a global phase.
>
> Allowed gates: rx ry rz h x y z s sdg sx sxdg p u cx rzz (and barrier).
> Each flip exp(-i a_p(Z_nb) X_p dt) is a uniformly controlled rotation on qubit p
> controlled by its neighbours (Gray-code construction: 2**(#neighbours) cx gates).

## Used by

`su2torus.mps` · `su2torus.noise`

`trotter_step`, `trotter_circuit`, `two_qubit_counts`

# skqd.basis

Module of [[su2qc-skqd]] · `src/skqd/basis.py` · 86 lines

## What it does (from the module docstring)

> Gauge-invariant configuration basis  |b> = |{j_l}, {n_x}, {iota_x}>  of the
> dressed-site construction (Step 2 of the SKQD manual), with baryon-number
> sectors.
>
> A label b is stored as (j2, n, iota): tuples of ints with j2 = 2 j_l per link,
> n = occupation per site, iota = intertwiner index per site.  The basis is the
> list of all labels for which every vertex has a non-empty singlet space, one
> state per choice of the intertwiner indices.
>
> Baryon number  B = 1/2 sum_x (n_x - n^vac_x),  n^vac_x = 0 on even sites and
> 2 on odd sites.  We store 2B as an int.

## Uses

[[skqd.lattice]] · [[skqd.vertex]]

title: skqd.circuits_cudaq
text:
# skqd.circuits_cudaq

Module of [[su2qc-skqd]] · `src/skqd/circuits_cudaq.py` · 154 lines

## What it does (from the module docstring)

> CUDA-Q translation of the IR circuits (circuits_ir.py) for GPU statevector
> sampling on the laptop (target 'nvidia', GTX 1060 Max-Q) or the desktop (RTX 3070).
>
> NOT executed in the cloud sandbox where this package was assembled.  The laptop
> gate scripts/laptop_L5_cudaq_check.py first establishes the two conventions that
> cannot be known without running CUDA-Q — the order of the result strings and the
> qubit order of cudaq.register_operation for multi-qubit matrices — with a CNOT
> test, and only then compares a sampled 2x2 circuit with the numpy reference.
>
> Design.  CUDA-Q compiles @cudaq.kernel functions from their Python source
> (inspect.getsource), so the IR gate list is turned into straight-line kernel
> SOURCE CODE written to a real .py file in a temporary directory and imported;
> custom unitaries (the hopping block unitaries) are registered first with
> cudaq.register_operation(name, matrix) and called by name inside the kernel, as
> in the CUDA-Q documentation example
>
>     cudaq.register_operation("custom_h", np.array([ [1, 1], [1, -1] ]) / np.sqrt(2))
>     @cudaq.kernel
>     def bell():
>         q = cudaq.qvector(2)
>         custom_h(q[0])
>         x.ctrl(q[0], q[1])
>
> Supported IR gates: x, h, rz, ry, rx, p (r1), cp, cx, gphase, unitary (1- and
> multi-qubit, via cudaq.register_operation) and mcu (a registered one-qubit
> operation applied with .ctrl, with X conjugation for controls active on |0>).
>
> Endianness.  BIG_ENDIAN = True means the first qubit argument of a registered
> operation is the MOST significant bit of its matrix; the matrices of this
> package are little-endian (first qubit = least significant bit, see
> reference_sim.py), so they are bit-reversed before registration when
> BIG_ENDIAN is True.  The convention test in the L5 script sets this flag from
> a measurement; the default below is only a guess.

## Public names

`kernel_source`, `build_kernel`, `sample`

## Concepts

[[Transpilation and CZ count]] · [[CUDA-Q]] · [[Laptop (Dell G7)]]

title: skqd.circuits_ir
text:
# skqd.circuits_ir

Module of [[su2qc-skqd]] · `src/skqd/circuits_ir.py` · 973 lines

## What it does (from the module docstring)

> Backend-independent circuit description ("IR") of the support-generating
> circuits, built from exact local block unitaries of the Hamiltonian terms.
> The IR is a list of gates (name, qubits, params):
>
>     ('x',  [q], None)                     Pauli X (state preparation)
>     ('h',  [q], None)
>     ('rz', [q], angle)                    Rz(angle) = exp(-i angle Z / 2)
>     ('p',  [q], angle)                    phase gate diag(1, e^{i angle})
>     ('cp', [c, t], angle)                 controlled phase diag(1,1,1,e^{i angle})
>     ('cx', [c, t], None)
>     ('unitary', qubits, U)                dense 2^k x 2^k unitary, qubits[0] = least significant bit
>
> Everything in this file is executed and verified in numpy (reference_sim.py);
> the Qiskit and CUDA-Q modules only translate the IR.
>
> Term gates for exp(-i theta H_gamma), gamma in {diag, hop_l, plaq_P}:
>   * diag: exact phases from n_x and j_l read from the codeword bits
>       corner:   n = (q1 xor q2) + 2 q3            (valid codewords)
>       interior: n = f + 2 q4 (1 - f), f = q1 xor q2 xor q3 (parity of the flux ends)
>       electric: (g^2/2) * 3/4 per flux link, applied once, on the 'out' end's flux qubit
>   * hop_l: dense local unitary on the support of reference_sim.term_support
>   * plaq_P: structured gate at 2x2 (corner-only plaquettes) with a Gray-code
>     uniformly controlled Rz; dense local unitary otherwise (only usable for
>     statevector simulation when the support has <= 12 qubits; larger supports
>     raise NotImplementedError until the S2-b decomposition exists).
>     Note: the structured gate equals the dense block unitary on the codeword
>     subspace but is NOT the identity on leaked (non-codeword) strings, whereas
>     the dense local unitary is; with noise the two differ on leaked states.
>
> Coarse single-step circuit (manual Step 4.3 b): X gates preparing the reference
> codeword, then the term gates with theta = k dt in the order diag, hop_0, hop_1,
> ..., plaq_0, ...  (same order as krylov.term_groups).  First-order Trotter: the
> same block repeated k times with theta = dt.
>
> Symbols: theta = angle, dt = Krylov step, k = coarse-step multiplier.

## Uses

[[skqd.codec]] · [[skqd.exact]] · [[skqd.krylov]] · [[skqd.reference_sim]]

## Public names

`gray`, `ucr_angles`, `ucr_gray`, `ucrz_gray`, `structured_term_gates`, `term_structure`, `CircuitFactory`, `run_ir`, `gate_counts`

## Concepts

title: skqd.codec
text:
# skqd.codec

Module of [[su2qc-skqd]] · `src/skqd/codec.py` · 202 lines

## What it does (from the module docstring)

> Hardware codewords and the per-shot decoder (Steps 2.4 and 2.5 of the SKQD manual).
>
> Qubit layout: vertices own contiguous blocks of qubits in site order; a bit
> string is a tuple of ints q_0 ... q_{N-1} (q_k = value of qubit k).  Within a
> vertex the first bits are the flux bits of its link ends in canonical (link
> index) order, j = 1/2 <=> 1.
>
> Corner (2 ends), 3 qubits (q1,q2,q3):
>     q1 = q2 -> n in {0,2}, q3 = n/2;    q1 != q2 -> n = 1, q3 = 0 (q3 = 1 is a leakage flag)
> Interior (3 ends), 4 qubits:
>     #flux ends even -> q4 = n/2;  one -> n = 1, q4 = 0 (q4 = 1 flag);  three -> n = 1, q4 = iota
> Charged corner (static spin-1/2), 3 qubits:
>     (0,0) -> n = 1, q3 = 0 (1 flag);  (1,1) -> n = 1, q3 = iota;  unequal -> n in {0,2}, q3 = n/2
> Charged interior, 5 qubits (17 states; the manual fixes the count, the bit
> assignment below is this package's choice):
>     #flux 0 -> n = 1, (q4,q5) = (0,0);   #flux 1 -> n in {0,2}, (q4,q5) = (n/2, 0);
>     #flux 2 -> n = 1, (q4,q5) = (iota, 0);  #flux 3 -> n in {0,2}, (q4,q5) = (n/2, iota);
>     every other (q4,q5) is a flag.
>
> Decoder: (i) split into vertex codewords, (ii) reject any flagged vertex,
> (iii) reject any link whose flux bit differs between its two end vertices,
> (iv) read ({j_l},{n_x},{iota_x}), (v) reject if sum_x n_x is not the target
> sector, (vi) look the label up in the basis index.
>
> Symbols: n = quark occupation, iota = intertwiner label, j = link spin.

`skqd.circuits_ir` · `skqd.hardware` · `skqd.noise` · `skqd.reference_sim`

title: skqd.coherence
text:
# skqd.coherence

Module of [[su2qc-skqd]] · `src/skqd/coherence.py` · 370 lines

## What it does (from the module docstring)

> Coherence requirement of a compiled circuit: what T2 a device must have to run it.
>
> `skqd.idle` answers "given a calibration record, what does the idle time of this schedule
> cost in log-error units".  This module inverts that question -- given a schedule and a
> target clean-shot fraction, what coherence time does the device need -- and puts the answer
> next to the closed-form estimate the owner uses for a nearly serial circuit,
>
>     T2 / t_2q  >=  n_qubits x n_2q / (2 ln(1/f_target))                       (`serial_bound`)
>
> which assumes (a) a perfectly serial circuit, T = n_2q t_2q, (b) every qubit idle for the
> whole of T, and (c) the linearised T2 term only (no T1 channel, no saturation of
> 1 - e^{-w/T2}).  On the frozen 2x2 canary (a) holds to 3 % and (b) does not: the qubit-time
> utilisation is 0.233 (`data/S2_duration_compare.json` rescheduling_headroom), so the qubits
> are idle 77 % of T rather than 100 %.  `t2_requirement` therefore solves the real budget of
> `skqd.idle` (a per-qubit sum over the ACTUAL idle windows of an ASAP schedule) by bisection,
> and the ratio of the two numbers is a measurement rather than an assumption.
>
> Nothing here is fitted and nothing here is a criterion.  Two conventions are always
> arguments of the call, never choices of this module:
>
> * **which T2**.  The bound is quoted as the dimensionless ratio T2 / t_2q; whether the
>   vendor's number is a Hahn-echo T2 or an in-circuit T2* is the vendor's to declare
>   (amendment 01 item 2, `skqd.idle`'s "Which T2" note).
> * **the T1 channel**.  `t1_mode="inf"` charges dephasing only (the serial formula's premise);
>   `t1_mode="equal"` sets T1 = T2, which is the pessimistic end for a device that quotes one
>   coherence number.
>
> `uniform_record` builds a calibration record in exactly the format
> `scripts/h0_backends.calibration_record` writes, so `skqd.idle` reads a synthetic uniform
> device and a real snapshot through the same code path.

# skqd.controls

Module of [[su2qc-skqd]] · `src/skqd/controls.py` · 97 lines

## What it does (from the module docstring)

> Classical-support controls at prescribed support size (Step 6 of the SKQD manual).
>
>   (a) CIPSI selected CI: start from the references; iterate {diagonalize on B,
>       score every Hamiltonian neighbour c not in B by |<c|H|psi_R>|^2 / (H_cc - E_R),
>       add the top batch} until |B| reaches the target.
>   (b) BFS neighbour growth, truncated at random when the next layer overshoots.
>   (c) random configurations of the sector (references always included).
>   (d) oracle: the top-|B| configurations by exact ground-state weight (simulator only).
>   (e) ML-alone: the top-|B| configurations by a learned score (ml.py).
>   (f) device-seeded CIPSI: CIPSI growth starting from a device support.
>
> All functions return sorted arrays of full-basis indices of exactly the target size
> (when the sector allows it).
>
> Symbols: B = support, N(B) = Hamiltonian neighbours, psi_R = Ritz vector,
> E_R = Ritz value, H_cc = diagonal element.

title: skqd.device_req
text:
# skqd.device_req

Module of [[su2qc-skqd]] · `src/skqd/device_req.py` · 243 lines

## What it does (from the module docstring)

> Device-requirement algebra for the amended budget criterion.
>
> The amended criterion (amendment 01, section 1(c); gate S2D) is a condition on the
> clean-shot fraction of a circuit executed on a device,
>
>     f = prod_{2q gates} (1 - eps2) x prod_{1q gates} (1 - eps1) x prod_{measured} (1 - eps_ro)
>       = (1 - eps2)^n_2q (1 - eps1)^n_1q (1 - eps_ro)^n_meas ,
>
> with `mean f >= 0.1` over the circuit set and `worst f >= 0.05`.  Gate S2D evaluates f at
> one declared error triple; this module inverts the same expression, so that a *requirement*
> can be stated as a region in (eps2, eps1, eps_ro) instead of a single number.
>
> Nothing here is a new physics model: `clean_shot_fraction` is the f of `gate_S2D.analyse_rzz`
> written as a function of the gate counts, and every inversion is exact.
>
> Two exact facts are used throughout.
>
> * f depends on the error triple only through the *log-error budget*: taking -log of the
>   expression above, f >= f_target is the half-space
>
>       n_2q eps2~ + n_1q eps1~ + n_meas eps_ro~ <= log(1 / f_target),   eps~ := -log(1 - eps),
>
>   linear in the log-errors eps~ (and, to first order in eps, in the errors themselves).
>   `log_error_budget` returns the weights and the budget of that half-space.
> * f is strictly decreasing in each error, so the requirement on one channel with the other
>   two fixed has a closed form (`required_error`), and the requirement that a *statistic* of f
>   over a circuit set reach a target is found by bisection (`required_error_for_set`).

# skqd.fermions

Module of [[su2qc-skqd]] · `src/skqd/fermions.py` · 48 lines

## What it does (from the module docstring)

> Two-colour staggered-fermion site.
>
> Local Fock space F = span{|n_1 n_2>} with the ordering (0,0), (1,0), (0,1), (1,1)
> (index c = n_1 + 2 n_2).  Local annihilators with the intra-site Jordan-Wigner
> sign:  psi_1 = a (x) 1,  psi_2 = P (x) a,  P = (-1)^n on one mode.
>
> Global operators on a chain of sites (JW ordering = site index order):
>     psi_{x,i} = (prod_{z<x} P_z) (x) psi^loc_{x,i},   P_z = (-1)^{n_z}.
>
> Matter charge  Q_a = psi^dag (sigma_a/2) psi  (see su2.py for why sigma_a/2 and
> not -sigma_a^T/2: it is tied to the convention L_a = -J_a^T, R_a = +J_a of the
> link generators).
>
> n = occupation number (0, 1, 2), c = Fock index, P = parity operator.

# skqd.fullspace

Module of [[su2qc-skqd]] · `src/skqd/fullspace.py` · 187 lines

## What it does (from the module docstring)

> Redundant-basis ("projector") construction of the 2 x 2 model — the second,
> independent route of gate E1 (Step 1.3 of the SKQD manual).
>
> The full Hilbert space is the tensor product of the four truncated link spaces
> (5 states each for jmax = 1/2) and the four site Fock spaces (4 states each):
> dimension 5^4 * 4^4 = 160 000.  All operators are built directly from the
> link operators U_ij, L_a, R_a and the fermion operators with explicit
> Jordan-Wigner strings, with no reference to the dressed-site tensors.
>
> Provided checks:
>   * [G_a(x), H] = 0 for every site x and colour a  (gauge invariance of H)
>   * the kernel of sum_{x,a} G_a(x)^2, computed block by block by dense
>     diagonalization (blocks = fixed link spins and site occupations), has
>     dimension 82 with baryon-number split 38/20/20/2/2
>   * P^dag H P on that kernel has the same spectrum as the dressed-site builder
>   * the dressed-site states embedded in the full space are annihilated by
>     every G_a(x), are orthonormal, and reproduce the builder's matrix
>     elements one by one (this tests the contraction formula, JW signs and
>     phases, not only the spectrum).
>
> Symbols: G_a(x) = Gauss-law generator at site x, P = isometry from the
> physical (kernel) space into the redundant space, H = Hamiltonian of
> hamiltonian.py.

[[skqd.basis]] · [[skqd.fermions]] · [[skqd.hamiltonian]] · [[skqd.lattice]] · [[skqd.su2]]

title: skqd.hamiltonian
text:
# skqd.hamiltonian

Module of [[su2qc-skqd]] · `src/skqd/hamiltonian.py` · 316 lines

## What it does (from the module docstring)

> Dressed-site Hamiltonian builder — Step 3 / Algorithm 2 of the SKQD manual.
>
> H = -1/2 sum_{l=(x->y)} [ eta_l psi^dag_{x,i} U_ij(l) psi_{y,j} + h.c. ]
>     + m sum_x (-1)^{x1+x2} n_x
>     + g^2/2 sum_l E_l^2
>     - 1/(2 g^2) sum_P (W_P + W_P^dag),
> W_P = sum_{ijkl} U_ij(l_b) U_jk(l_r) (U_lk(l_t))^dag (U_il(l_l))^dag  (counter-clockwise
> from the lower-left corner), links truncated at jmax in the electric basis.
>
> Matrix elements between dressed-site states are obtained by local contraction
> (eq. 4 of the manual): the local singlet tensors of the touched vertices, the
> link operator blocks, the site Fock operators, and the Jordan-Wigner sign
> s_JW = prod_{x<z<y} (-1)^{n_z} for a hopping term psi^dag_x psi_y with the
> intra-site signs absorbed into F_x = psi^loc_dag_{x,i} P_x and F_y = psi^loc_{y,j}
> (x < y, which always holds for the ladder's link orientation).
>
> The builder returns the term matrices separately:
>     terms['mass']      : diag  sum_x (-1)^{x1+x2} n_x
>     terms['electric']  : diag  sum_l j_l (j_l + 1)
>     terms['hop'][l]    : -(eta_l/2) sum_ij psi^dag_x U_ij psi_y + h.c.   (one per link)
>     terms['plaq'][P]   : W_P + W_P^dag                                    (one per plaquette)
> and  H(g^2, m) = m*mass + (g^2/2)*electric + sum_l hop[l] - 1/(2 g^2) sum_P plaq[P].
>
> Symbols: g^2 = gauge coupling, m = staggered quark mass, eta_l = staggered
> hopping phase, E_l^2 = j_l(j_l+1) electric Casimir, n_x = quark occupation.

title: skqd.hardware
text:
# skqd.hardware

Module of [[su2qc-skqd]] · `src/skqd/hardware.py` · 211 lines

## What it does (from the module docstring)

> Hardware-session helpers (manual Step 9.1, prompts/07 and prompts/13).
>
> Two independent jobs:
>
> 1. **Readout calibration.**  `confusion_matrix` turns the counts of the
>    preparation circuits (all-0, all-1 and the single-qubit flips) into a
>    *tensored* (independent-qubit) readout model C with
>    ``C[q, m, p] = P(measure m on qubit q | prepared p)``, and `apply_inverse`
>    unfolds a counts dictionary with the exact tensor inverse
>    ``(C_0^{-1} x ... x C_{n-1}^{-1})``.  The tensored model ignores measurement
>    crosstalk between qubits; it is the model the SKQD manual's Step 9.1 asks for
>    ("per-qubit readout confusion") and it is the only one that can be calibrated
>    with O(n) circuits.  Unfolded counts are quasi-counts: they may be negative.
>
> 2. **Layout bookkeeping of a transpiled circuit.**  A transpiled circuit lives on
>    physical qubits and its routing permutes them, so its statevector is *not* in
>    this package's logical bit order.  `transpiled_layout` reads the final layout
>    and the measurement map off the circuit, and `logical_statevector` returns the
>    noiseless statevector of the transpiled circuit permuted back to logical order
>    (qubit k = bit k, `reference_sim`), which is what `CodewordEmbedding.leakage`
>    expects.  A wrong layout permutation is exactly the mistake that makes a real
>    hardware run decode to garbage, so it is checked before anything is submitted.
>
> `codeword_bit_order` and `link_consistency_checks` export the decoder's own
> bookkeeping (which qubit carries which vertex/link datum, and which qubit pairs
> must agree) into the per-circuit manifests that travel with the job.
>
> Nothing here changes a convention; `codec.py` and `reference_sim.py` are read only.

title: skqd.idle
text:
# skqd.idle

Module of [[su2qc-skqd]] · `src/skqd/idle.py` · 270 lines

## What it does (from the module docstring)

> Idle-time relaxation in the clean-shot fraction f.
>
> `gate_S2D.analyse_on_backend` (and `device_req.clean_shot_fraction`, its inverse algebra)
> computes f as a product over the *instructions* of a compiled circuit,
>
>     f_gates = prod_{2q gates} (1 - eps_gate) x prod_{measured qubits} (1 - eps_ro) ,
>
> and therefore contains no term for the time a qubit spends WAITING for other qubits'
> gates.  On a heavy-hex device the routed 2x2 coarse step is nearly serial (663 CZ in
> depth 1328, 43.71 us before readout) and each of its 12 qubits idles 19-42 us of that;
> the omission is not small.  Gate H0_diag (2026-09-22, `validation/H0_diag.json`) measured
> the canary circuit under {DD on/off} x {twirling on/off} and found f = 0.0255 where
> `analyse_on_backend` predicted 0.2195, with the idle term accounting for the whole
> discrepancy (3.323 error units available against 2.153 missing).
>
> This module adds that term, with no fitted parameter.  It schedules a compiled circuit
> ASAP on a calibration RECORD (`scripts/h0_backends.calibration_record`: the record's own
> durations, T1, T2 and errors), collects the idle windows of every active qubit, and
> converts them into a log-error budget in the Pauli-twirling approximation of thermal
> relaxation -- the channel Aer's `RelaxationNoisePass` would attach to an explicit `delay`:
>
>     per idle window w on qubit q:   p = (1 - e^{-w/T1_q})/4 + (1 - e^{-w/T2_q})/2
>     S_T1 = sum_q sum_w (1 - e^{-w/T1_q})/4     S_T2 = sum_q sum_w (1 - e^{-w/T2_q})/2
>     f    = f_gates x exp(-S_T1 - S_T2)                                   (DD off)
>
> The runtime's `PadDynamicalDecoupling` pads a window only when it is longer than
> `sequence_min_length_ratios` (default 2.0) times the sequence length, so with XY4 =
> 4 x sx_duration a window is DD-eligible when w / (4 sx_duration) > 2.0, and one sequence
> per eligible window costs S_DD = sum_eligible 4 x sx_error.  The refocusing efficiency
> rho (the fraction of the eligible-window T2 budget that survives DD) is not computable
> from a calibration, so DD-on predictions are a bracket over rho:
>
>     f(rho) = f_gates x exp(-S_T1 - rho S_T2_eligible - S_T2_ineligible - S_DD) .
>
> **Which T2.**  The calibration record's `T2_s` is the vendor's Hahn-echo T2; the windowed
> Ramsey test of gate H0_diag measured the free-induction T2* on the same patch on the same
> day and found it 2-7x shorter (median ratio 0.174 over the 9 qubits with a usable time).
> Neither is the effective dephasing time inside a circuit, and H0_diag does not determine
> where between them it lies: on the echo T2 the idle-aware model predicted 31 accepted
> shots against the measured 35 (a factor 1.13), on the measured T2* it is 89x too
> pessimistic.  This module therefore never chooses: `idle_budget` takes an explicit
> per-qubit `t2_s` override and `effective_t2` builds one from a recorded ratio, so the
> convention is always an argument of the call and a recorded field of the output.
>
> Nothing here is a criterion and nothing here is fitted.  The bars of amendment 01
> section 1(c) (mean f >= 0.1, worst f >= 0.05) are unchanged; what changes is the f they
> are read on.

`skqd.coherence`

# skqd.krylov

Module of [[su2qc-skqd]] · `src/skqd/krylov.py` · 191 lines

## What it does (from the module docstring)

> Support-generating states (Step 4 of the SKQD manual), emulated exactly in
> the gauge-invariant basis.
>
>   * exact Krylov states      |psi_k> = exp(-i k H dt) |b0>,  k = 0 .. d-1
>   * first-order Trotter      |psi_k> = [ prod_gamma exp(-i H_gamma dt) ]^k |b0>
>   * coarse single-step       |psi_k> =   prod_gamma exp(-i H_gamma k dt)   |b0>   (one step per circuit)
> with the term groups gamma = diagonal (mass + electric), one group per hopping
> link, one per plaquette, applied in that order (the order is a convention of
> this package; it matters for the Trotterised and coarse states, not for the
> exact Krylov states).
>
> Reference configurations (Step 4.2): the Dirac sea, the one-meson
> configurations (quark on the even end, hole on the odd end, flux on the link),
> the diquark on each even site (B = 1), and for static sectors the flux string
> along the bottom row plus its one-plaquette deformations.
>
> Symbols: dt = pi / W_B Krylov time step, d = number of Krylov states,
> b0 = reference configuration, H_gamma = term group.
